Where it began

Shoaib Malik was born in Sialkot on 1 February 1982 and learned the game playing tape-ball cricket in the streets. At 12 he went along to a travelling coaching clinic in his home town and began to take it seriously, first as a batter and later as a bowler too. His family would rather he had kept his head in his books, but by 1996 he was in trials for Pakistan's Under-15 World Cup squad, and he was picked for his bowling.

He admired Saqlain Mushtaq so much that he rebuilt his off-spin to look like his hero's. His first-class career began with Gujranwala in 1997, and he moved on to the PIA side, where he shared a dressing room with Wasim Akram and Saqlain himself. His brother Adeel became a cricketer too.

The player

He first played for Pakistan in a one-day match in 1999 and made his Test debut against Bangladesh in 2001. Over 35 Tests, the last in 2015, he made 1,898 runs at 35.15, with 3 hundreds and a best of 245, and took 32 wickets with his off-breaks. His most famous Test innings came against Sri Lanka in 2006, when he batted through a whole day to save the match and finished with 148 not out.

In April 2007, aged 25, he was made Pakistan captain, the fourth-youngest man to hold the job, and he led the side for two years. In the white-ball game he was part of the Pakistan teams that won the World Twenty20 in 2009 and the Champions Trophy in 2017.

What made him special

He was the man for every job. In Tests he batted in five different places, opening when Pakistan were short of a pair, and in one-day cricket he batted in every position except number 11. He could hit hard, once making 82 from 41 balls against South Africa, but he was just as happy nudging singles into the gaps.

His off-spin was the junior partner. It was steady and useful in one-day games, but in Tests each of his 32 wickets cost a fair few runs, at 47.47 apiece.

Away from the middle

Few players have packed a bat for so many countries. He played county cricket for Gloucestershire and Warwickshire, and T20 cricket in Australia, the Caribbean, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Canada and India. He captained sides in the Pakistan Super League and stepped away from it in January 2026 after 93 matches and 2,350 runs. From 2021 he launched a perfume, made cameo appearances as an actor and hosted television shows.

And finally

The perfume he launched was called All Rounder. For a man who batted almost everywhere and bowled whenever asked, it is hard to think of a better name.
